title: Restriction to a localized ringed site preserves K-injectivity with independent coefficient universe
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with Grothendieck topology $J$, $\mathcal R$ a sheaf of rings with section modules in universe $\max(u,v,r)$, and $U\in\mathcal C$. Let $I$ be a K-injective cochain complex of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Its termwise restriction $I|_U$ to $\mathcal C/U$ is K-injective. Restriction sends zero morphisms to zero; its proof is an explicit parameter used only to form the functor on complexes. This universe-general form takes C : Type u with Category v and coefficient/module universe max u v r, for arbitrary r; assume abelian-group sheafification and its locally bijective characterization on the original site. It uses the same sheaves, restriction, Hom complex, differentials, and induced maps as the original source statement.

proof.text: Work with objects in Type u, arrows in Type v, and coefficient rings and modules in Type (max u v r). Use the existing siteAbelianHasSheafify and siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective instances on the slice whenever an abelian or exactness instance is needed. All these instances are proved, and the given base-site instances are retained.

Use the exact additive finite-limit and finite-colimit left adjunction supplied by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction]. The adjunction induces preservation of K-injective complexes by its right adjoint, so applying that preservation theorem to I yields K-injectivity after restriction.
